title: Marguerite and the Atlas
premise: In 1789 Lyon, census taker Elias Vane records a household that officially does not exist — and finds its ledger of names matches a list of men condemned by a magistrate who has never held trial. The print shop's daughter, Paloma Thackeray, cuts him a hidden typeface to duplicate the evidence, but every checkpoint between them and Paris is watched by the magistrate's own clerk. As the century turns on New Year's Eve, Elias must choose between burning the atlas to save Paloma's family or delivering it and letting history finally happen to him.
about_author: Isandro Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing provincial French censuses before turning to fiction. He writes from a farmhouse in the Dordogne, where he claims the ink is better.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Elias Vane, POV. A routine census visit to Thackeray & Sons Print Works turns when Elias asks for the name of the apprentice listed last year — a boy no one remembers hiring. Paloma deflects, but her father's trembling hands betray fear. Elias leaves with one extra name inked into his margins. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into unease; the sense of a door opening that cannot be shut.

chapters.title: Marguerite Cut Small
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. She discovers her father has been printing forged death certificates for men still alive, using a secret typeface she cut as a child and named Marguerite. When the magistrate's clerk arrives searching the shop, Paloma hides the type box inside the census atlas itself. Emotional beat: loyalty to her father warring with the truth pressing at her throat; first taste of complicity.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. Armed with the atlas and Paloma's duplicated pages, Elias travels toward Paris through river tolls, a garrison gate, and a cathedral checkpoint where the clerk waits with his portrait. At the second barrier he must decide whether to trust a stranger who recognizes Marguerite's letterforms. Emotional beat: rising dread and unexpected solidarity; justice revealed as something carried by hand, not granted by law.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs converge in Paris on New Year's Eve. The clerk corners Elias above the printing house where the evidence will be set; Paloma arrives with the original Marguerite type and trades her father's silence for publication. The atlas goes out with the morning edition as bells ring in 1790. Emotional beat: sacrifice transmuted into witness — memory, once printed, can no longer be erased.
